name: norm_realInner_realHeisOp_le
summary: Write the coefficient as an integral over C^iota; bound the multiplier by |sigma|^|iota| and the integrand pointwise by (|v(x/c)|^2 + |v((sigma x + y)/c)|^2) times (4(A+n)|sigma|^2/|y|^2)^n / c^(2|iota|) / 2 with c = sqrt(n/A + 1). Both summands integrate to c^(2|iota|) Re<v, v> (the second is the first composed with the measure-preserving map x -> sigma x + y), so the factor 2 and c^(2|iota|) cancel. The pointwise bound: |v(z)| = c^d |v(z/c)| exp(-n|z|^2/(2(A+n))) at z = x and z = sigma x + y (homogeneity and the Gaussian), 2ab <= a^2 + b^2, then with S = |x|^2 + |sigma x + y|^2 the scalar c^(2(d+|iota|)) exp(-nS/(2(A+n))) is at most e^(n(1-t)) <= t^(-n), t = S/(2(A+n)) (by 1 + u <= e^u, d + |iota| <= A and t <= e^(t-1)), and |y|^2 <= 2|sigma|^2 S (triangle inequality, |sigma| >= 1).

steps.claim: Let c = sqrt(n/A + 1), a real number >= 1.

i: the dilated function x -> |v(x/c)|^2 is integrable (|v|^2 is integrable, v being in the reproducing space of the vacuum, and c^(-1) is nonzero); p: the map T(x) = sigma x + y (the action of sigma followed by the translation by y) is measure preserving.
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨i, p⟩ := (integrable_norm_sq v).comp_smul (R := c⁻¹) (by positivity),
    ((realAction ε).2 σ).add_left _ y

steps.claim: j: x -> |v((sigma x + y)/c)|^2 is integrable: it is the dilated function x -> |v(x/c)|^2 of i composed with the measure-preserving map T(x) = sigma x + y of p (the composition of an integrable function with a measure-preserving map is integrable).

Write <v, rho(y) omega(sigma) v> as an integral over x in C^iota of the multiplier of sigma times conj(v) times the translated and rotated v (map_integrated_eq_integral, the definition of the Weil representation).
steps.lean:
rw [← (realInner v).comp_apply]; simp [↓map_integrated_eq_integral, weilRep, realAction,
    modelInner_self]

steps.claim: Bound the multiplier by |sigma|^|iota| and the integral by the integral of (|v(x/c)|^2 + |v((sigma x + y)/c)|^2) (4(A + n)(|sigma|/|y|)^2)^n / (c^2)^|iota| / 2 (integrable by i and j); it remains to prove this bound pointwise.
steps.lean:
grw [norm_realMultiplier_le, norm_integral_le_of_norm_le ((i.add j).mul_const ((4 * (A + n) *
    (‖σ.1.1‖ / ‖toLp 2 y‖) ^ 2) ^ n / (c ^ 2) ^ card ι / 2)) (.of_forall ?_)]

steps.claim: Integrate the bound. Both summands have the same integral c^(2|iota|) Re<v, v>: the second is the first composed with the measure-preserving map T, so it has the integral of the first, and the change of variables x -> x/c (a real space of dimension 2|iota|) gives c^(2|iota|) times the integral of |v|^2, which is Re<v, v>. The integral of the bound is therefore 2 c^(2|iota|) Re<v, v> (4(A + n)(|sigma|/|y|)^2)^n / (c^2)^|iota| / 2 = (4(A + n))^n |sigma|^(2n) |y|^(-2n) Re<v, v> (the factor 2 and c^(2|iota|) cancel); with the bound |sigma|^|iota| on the multiplier this is the right side of the statement.
steps.lean:
simp [mul_comm _ 2, ↓integral_mul_const, ↓integral_add' i j, ↓p.hasLaw.integral_comp i.1, mul_pow,
    pow_mul, ← two_mul, ↓Measure.integral_comp_inv_smul _ (‖v ·‖ ^ 2), div_pow, pow_add, field]

steps.claim: Pointwise, at x. For every z, |v(z/c)| = |v(z)| exp(|z|^2/(2(n + A)))^n / c^d, that is |v(z)| = c^d |v(z/c)| exp(-n|z|^2/(2(A + n))): P is homogeneous of degree d and the Gaussian factor gains exp(|z|^2 (1 - 1/c^2)/2) with 1 - 1/c^2 = n/(n + A). By the reproducing property the integrand has absolute value at most |v(x)| |v(sigma x + y)|; by 2ab <= a^2 + b^2 with a = |v(x/c)|, b = |v((sigma x + y)/c)| it suffices that |v(x)| |v(sigma x + y)| <= |v(x/c)| |v((sigma x + y)/c)| (4(A + n)(|sigma|/|y|)^2)^n / c^(2|iota|).
steps.lean:
simp_intro x [fun x ↦ (by simp (disch := positivity) [*, realVac, star_dot_self_eq_norm_sq, sq, c,
    ← exp_nat_mul, mul_assoc, ← exp_add, field, star_trivial] : ‖v (c⁻¹ • x)‖ = ‖v x‖ * exp
    (‖toLp 2 x‖ ^ 2 / (n + A) / 2) ^ n / |c| ^ d), ↓modelInner_heisOp_vacElem,
    ← conj_modelInner]; grw [← two_mul_le_add_sq]

steps.claim: Collect the powers and exponentials. Write k = |iota| and S = |x|^2 + |sigma x + y|^2. Expressing both |v(x/c)| and |v((sigma x + y)/c)| through |v(x)| and |v(sigma x + y)| (step 7), the powers of c combine to c^(2(d + k)) and the two Gaussian factors to exp(nS/(2(A + n))); what remains is the scalar bound c^(2(d + k)) exp(-nS/(2(A + n))) <= (4(A + n) |sigma|^2/|y|^2)^n (the common factor |v(x)| |v(sigma x + y)| >= 0 is cancelled by the monotonicity step of step 9).
steps.lean: simp [field, pow_right_comm _ d, mul_assoc, ← pow_add, ← mul_pow, ← exp_add]

steps.claim: c^2 = n/A + 1 <= e^(n/A) (1 + t <= e^t), so c^(2(d + k)) <= e^(n(d + k)/A) <= e^n because d + k <= A (hA, k = |iota|). Put t = S/(2(A + n)) > 0. Then e^n exp(-nS/(2(A + n))) = e^(n(1 - t)), and e t <= e^t (that is, t <= e^(t - 1)) gives e^(n(1 - t)) <= t^(-n) = (2(A + n)/S)^n. After cancelling the positive factors (gcongr) and clearing denominators, it remains to show |y|^2 <= 2 |sigma|^2 S.
steps.lean:
grw [sq_sqrt (by bound), add_one_le_exp, ← exp_nat_mul, hA, mul_div_left_comm,
    div_self_le_one, exp_nat_mul, ← exp_one_mul_le_exp]; gcongr; field_simp

steps.claim: |y| <= |sigma x + y| + |sigma x| <= |sigma x + y| + |sigma| |x| (triangle inequality and the operator norm) <= |sigma| (|sigma x + y| + |x|) because |sigma| >= 1; with (a + b)^2 <= 2(a^2 + b^2) this gives |y|^2 <= 2 |sigma|^2 (|x|^2 + |sigma x + y|^2) = 2 |sigma|^2 S, which concludes.
steps.lean:
grw [norm_le_add_norm_add, σ.1.1.l2_opNorm_mulVec (toLp 2 x), ← one_mul ‖_ + _‖,
    U.one_le_norm σ, add_sq_le]; linarith!
